en: The carabao, the Philippine national animal, is a domesticated swamp buffalo used by farmers to plow rice paddies.
The Sampaguita, the national flower of the Philippines, is a fragrant white jasmine often woven into floral garlands.
Dr. Fe del Mundo invented a bamboo incubator to provide premature babies with warmth in rural areas without electricity.
The Supreme Court, located in Manila, is the highest court in the Philippines and leads the judicial branch of government.
The Ifugao people built the Banaue Rice Terraces by carving steps into the mountains of the Cordilleras over two thousand years ago.
The Philippine eagle, the national bird, is a critically endangered raptor with a distinctive shaggy crest found only in Mindanao.
Emilio Aguinaldo proclaimed Philippine independence from Spain on June 12, 1898, from the window of his house in Kawit, Cavite.
Filipino, the national language, is primarily based on Tagalog but incorporates words from other Philippine languages and foreign dialects.
Jose Rizal wrote the novels Noli Me Tangere and El Filibusterismo to expose the abuses of the Spanish colonial government.
During the Sinulog festival in Cebu, dancers perform a rhythmic forward-and-backward step to honor the Santo Niño.
Under the Philippine Constitution, every citizen has the duty to pay correct taxes and the right to receive basic education.
The Narra, the national tree of the Philippines, is a hardy hardwood species known for its durable and termite-resistant wood.
